title: Tesla target lowered by analysts worried about runaway $25 billion spending
detail:
Tesla target lowered by analysts worried about runaway $25 billion spending
Tony Owusu, Dana Sullivan Kilroy
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 2:33 PM MDT 5 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

At the top of the year, Tesla let Wall Street know that 2026 would not be a regular year for the company.

Fresh off its second consecutive year of falling deliveries in 2025, the company and its stock were at a crossroads. So Tesla's announcement that it was raising its capital expenditure plan to above $25 billion was a bit of a surprise.

"While this may seem substantial, and we will face negative free cash flow impacts for the remainder of the year, we believe this is the right strategic approach to position the company for its next era," Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja said at the time.

Also read: Why your next car purchase will be an affordability nightmare

Tesla plans to spend the money on improving its artificial intelligence while also repurposing production lines formerly designated for the now-defunct Model S and Model X for production of Optimus, its humanoid robot.

But negative cash flow is enough to make any investor nervous, and analysts at BNP Paribas, who are already bearish on the stock, lowered their price targets on concerns about the money Tesla is spending.

BNP Paribas lowers Tesla price target

Analysts at BNP Paribas lowered Tesla's price target to $266 per share from $268 per share this week in a note viewed by TheStreet.

Additionally, the firm lowered its 2026 sales estimate by 2%. The new forecast comes after Tesla's third-quarter deliveries fell short of its expectations, and concerns about the company's spending persist. The new price target represents a 30% downside from Tesla's trading level on Monday, Oct. 12.

¨We view cash burn as a critical 'reality check' each qtr.," analysts said, while noting that Tesla's AI division has only produced 169 Cybercabs in Austin and the zero Optimus robots for sale so far. ¨Despite Tesla's $30 billion in secured funding, we see the potential for Capex and liquidity needs to run substantially higher vs. our $27.5 billion/$29 billion forecast for 2027 and 2028.¨

Robert Alexander / Getty Images
Deutsche Bank analysts go the other way

Wall Street's take on Tesla isn't monolithic, with Deutsche Bank analysts recently raising their price target 11% to $420 per share from $370.59, representing an 11% increase after the company topped the bank's own third-quarter delivery estimate by more than 5%.

The firm was particularly impressed with the company's international performance. 

"Our sense is upside came from Europe being stronger in September (e.g., France, Sweden) and China also outperforming, helped by cash discounts on in-stock cars; we think U.S. demand remained supply constrained with Model Y and Model Y L wait times running into 2027," Yu said.

title: Cathie Wood sells Meta shares after Zuckerberg's big AI launch

Cathie Wood sells Meta shares after Zuckerberg's big AI launch
Anand Sinha
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 12:48 PM MDT 2 min read
META
SPCX
TSLA
BTC-USD
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood is one of the most aggressive investors when it comes to emerging technologies.

Whether it's cryptocurrency or artificial intelligence (AI), she doesn't hesitate to bet big. In fact, she is one of the earliest investors in Bitcoin (BTC) and Elon Musk's tech babies SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX) and Tesla (Nasdaq: TSLA).

But she doesn't shy away from trimming her stake in a stock if need be, and she did exactly that with Meta Platforms (Nasdaq: META) yesterday even as the tech giant launched new AI products.

Cathie Wood trims stake in Meta

On Oct. 12, ARK Invest sold 4,520 Meta shares worth approximately $3.4 million as Mark Zuckerberg made a major AI announcement.

Meta CEO announced Monday the launch of Muse Wonder models for personal and professional agentic work.

Muse is Meta's AI agent built to execute multi-step tasks across the internet and apps on the user's behalf. It can answer questions, complete tasks, browse the web, make purchases, generate images, create documents, set reminders, and track goals.

While Muse Wonder drives fast frontier performance, Muse Wonder Full is its full version.

Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive officer of Meta Platforms Inc., exits Los Angeles Superior Court in Los Angeles, California, U.S., on Wednesday, Feb. 18, 2026. Getty Images
Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

Treasury Secretary Bessent drops a new bombshell on Iran

Ripple takes on Wall Street banks with a $35 billion client

Wall Street's youngest CEO of his day predicts $1M Bitcoin

The latest launches show Zuckerberg is still very much involved in the race with AI giants like Anthropic and OpenAI.

The META stock opened yesterday at $728.50 and hit as high as $752.24 following the announcement. The stock closed Monday at $742.96.

Meta Platforms stock, Source: Yahoo Finance

But Wood decided to trim her stake in the company's stock despite the surge.

Wood sold Meta shares worth $14.3 million on Oct. 8 as well. But these are the only two Meta sales by ARK Invest in recent weeks.

Data from the Cathie's ARK tracker shows that the investment firm has been loading up on Meta shares for months now.

In fact, Wood's firm bought $73.6 million in Meta shares last month as the Big Tech company rolled out its flagship Muse AI product.

The META stock was trading at around $760 at the time of writing, up 2.39% in a day.

title: Tesla Trades at 219x Earnings. Here’s Why I’m Not Buying the Bet on Its Future.
detail:
Tesla Trades at 219x Earnings. Here’s Why I’m Not Buying the Bet on Its Future.
Jabran Kundi
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:15 AM MDT 3 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As of October 12, Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares have climbed about 3% over the past five days. The rally began after Q3 deliveries came in at 486,532, well above the roughly 462,000 analysts expected. Deliveries were still down about 2% from a year earlier, though. More European countries have also approved Tesla's supervised FSD software. Even after the bounce, the stock is down about 15% this year. All eyes are now on its Q3 earnings, due October 21. TSLA's next catalyst may be earnings, but its longer-term prospects are worth watching too. See why Tesla ranks third among 10 stocks that could change the world by 2030.

Tesla Trades at 219x Earnings. Here’s Why I’m Not Buying the Bet on Its Future.
Investors Are Buying the Future

On October 6, Goldman Sachs made a point I agree with. It said Tesla's stock will move more on robotaxi, FSD, and Optimus updates than on quarterly earnings. Goldman kept a Neutral rating with a $360 price target, below where the stock trades today. That says a lot about how the market values Tesla. The car business is barely growing, yet the stock trades as if robotaxis and robots are already working at scale. Tesla has started putting its Cybercab into limited service in Austin. But Waymo already completes over 500,000 paid rides a week across 15 U.S. cities, so Tesla still has a lot of ground to cover. The company has big ambitions in autonomous driving and robotics, but how does it compare with ARK Invest's other high-conviction picks?

The Valuation Asks Investors to Wait Until 2029

Tesla's valuation is hard to defend on current earnings. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 219.06x sits about 81% above its 5-year average of 121.30x. The forward Price-to-sales ratio of 14.08x is also about 35% above its average of 10.41x. With multiples that high, you'd expect the EPS trajectory to be exceptional. But analysts expect growth of just 5% in 2026 and 23% in 2027. The big jumps only come later, with growth of 51% in 2028 and 101% in 2029. Even based on 2029 earnings, the P/E would still be about 59x. Tesla held about $34.4 billion more in cash and short-term investments than outstanding debt at the end of Q2, providing financial flexibility for its AI investments. Still, the stock leaves little room for delays, and robotaxi timelines have slipped before.

Fewer hedge funds held Tesla in Q2, with the count falling from 123 in Q1 to 116 in Q2. The value of their stakes, though, edged up from $23.1 billion to $23.8 billion.

Tesla's future could be huge if robotaxis and Optimus deliver. But based on the numbers, I don't think the stock is worth buying at this price. Investors are paying today for earnings that may not arrive until 2029, and even then the stock wouldn't look cheap.

What is the best way to figure out how high a stock can trade? One answer is to look at how high it has traded in the past. That at least shows that, at its best, a company reached a pinnacle of valuation. If the right pieces fall into place, it should be able to return to that level. Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) has made an extraordinary comeback in its core EV business. The stock traded at $490 last December. It trades at $375 today. To retake that summit, shares will rise 30%.

The broadest measure of Tesla's success showed up most recently in China, the world's largest EV market by far. Deliveries there rose 5% year over year to 95,366. Some of these were exported to Europe and North America. This happened amid a sharp weakening in the Chinese EV business overall.

Granada / Wikimedia Commons

Tesla's recovery in the EU is more impressive. After a beating sales took, perhaps because of the relationship between CEO Elon Musk and President Trump, the rebound has been extraordinary. In the first eight months of the year, Tesla's EU sales have risen 65.9% to 142,165, based on data from the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association.

And Tesla's EV market share in the US has moved back above 50%. It fell sharply, again probably due to Musk's brief government efficiency partnership with Donald Trump.
